answer: The ambiguity regarding the classification of predictive maintenance products as safety components under the AI Act arises from the uncertainty about whether, if these products fail, traditional quality assurance mechanisms will still be activated. If these mechanisms do activate upon failure, the products would presumably not be considered safety components. However, as trust in predictive maintenance products increases, it is likely that such quality assurance mechanisms may be dismantled, leading to the conclusion that these products could then be classified as safety components. This consideration is not adequately addressed by the AI Act.
